# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ieee20305/server"
```

Package server implements an IEEE 2030.5 server as an http.Handler. It manages device registration, DER programs and controls, event lifecycle, metering, and certificate-based access control.

The server authenticates devices by their client certificate, derives the LFDI from the certificate fingerprint, and enforces access control based on device identity. It serves XML resource representations over HTTPS with mutual TLS.

The operator tells the server of its devices with Admin.ProvisionDevice: their edition, their Role (a device, an aggregator that manages others, or an operator's head-end) and their registration PIN. The server creates the EndDevice of a device with its resources. With Config.InBandRegistration, an unknown device registers itself by posting its EndDevice, and Admin.Register registers it later.

With Config.NotificationClient, devices subscribe to resources and lists: every change made through the server, Admin or Store marks the subscriptions of the resource, and a worker per subscription posts the resource as it is then. Bursts of changes coalesce into the latest state, which arrives at least once and never before an older one. Delivery is retried with backoff, and the subscription cancelled when it keeps failing.

A resource comes with its parts: a DERProgram with its DERControlList, ActiveDERControlList, DERCurveList and DefaultDERControl, say. The server keeps the EventStatus of events as they become active, computes the Active lists and the CurrentDERProgram of a DER, and stores each Response once (Config.OnResponse); Admin.CancelEvent cancels an event.

A device mirrors its metering by posting a MirrorUsagePoint, which the server mirrors to a UsagePoint, and MirrorMeterReadings, which become its MeterReadings, ReadingTypes, ReadingSets and Readings, one per mRID. A FlowReservationRequest is answered by Config.FlowPolicy with a FlowReservationResponse event of the device.

A document the server sends has its href, its ListLinks the number of items the client reads (the all attribute), and no link to a resource of the server that does not exist yet (such as the DefaultDERControl of a program without one); a link to a resource the client creates with PUT stays.

## Functions

### func DefaultNotificationURIAllowed

```go
func DefaultNotificationURIAllowed(u *url.URL) bool
```

DefaultNotificationURIAllowed is the NotificationURIAllowed of a server without one: it refuses the hosts a device must not make the server connect to with its certificate: localhost, and literal loopback, unspecified, link-local and multicast addresses (cloud metadata services are link-local), with or without an IPv6 zone. It also refuses hosts whose last label is a number, such as 127.1, 2130706433 or 0x7f000001: they are no DNS names (RFC 1123, section 2.1), and the system resolver of some platforms reads them as IPv4 addresses (inet\_aton). A host name is not resolved: what the names of a network reach is for the operator's own NotificationURIAllowed, or its network, to decide.

GrantAll is the FlowPolicy that grants every request in full.

### func NewNotificationClient

```go
func NewNotificationClient(server tls.Certificate, deviceCAs *x509.CertPool) *http.Client
```

NewNotificationClient returns an http.Client for Config.NotificationClient: it presents the server's certificate, and verifies the listeners of the devices against deviceCAs (security.NotificationTLSConfig). It sets no timeout of its own: the notifier bounds each delivery with its context.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Store holds the resources; NewMemStore when nil.
	Store Store
	// Clock is the time of the server; time.Now when nil.
	Clock func() time.Time
	// Profile is the profile of the documents; StandardProfile when nil.
	Profile *Profile
	// DefaultEdition is the edition of IEEE 2030.5 the server speaks to a
	// client whose device record does not say (see DeviceSpec.Edition).
	DefaultEdition ieee20305.Edition
	// PeerCertificates returns the certificate chain of the client of a
	// request: by default r.TLS.PeerCertificates. A TLS stack whose
	// connections are not *crypto/tls.Conn (such as the CCM_8 module)
	// supplies its own.
	PeerCertificates func(r *http.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error)
	// MaxRequestBytes limits the size of a request body; 1 MiB when zero.
	MaxRequestBytes int64
	// DefaultLimit is the number of items of a list page when the request
	// gives no l parameter: 1, as IEEE 2030.5 specifies, when zero.
	DefaultLimit uint32
	// MaxLimit caps the l parameter; 255 when zero.
	MaxLimit uint32
	// EnableDiscouraged lists, by WADL resource ID, the methods the WADL
	// discourages that the server supports nonetheless.
	EnableDiscouraged map[string][]string
	// Disable lists, by WADL resource ID, methods the server refuses
	// although the WADL makes them mandatory or optional.
	Disable map[string][]string
	// InBandRegistration lets a device the server was not given
	// (Admin.ProvisionDevice) register itself by posting its EndDevice to the
	// EndDeviceList. The server creates its resources, without a
	// Registration until Admin.Register.
	InBandRegistration bool
	// ClientLists names, by WADL resource ID, lists of every client that
	// clients may post to, besides MirrorUsagePointList and ResponseList.
	ClientLists map[string]bool
	// PollRate is the pollRate of DeviceCapability, in seconds; 900 when
	// zero.
	PollRate uint32
	// NotificationClient sends the notifications of subscriptions, with the
	// certificate of the server as its client certificate. Without one the
	// server takes no subscriptions.
	NotificationClient *http.Client
	// NotificationURIAllowed decides whether the server sends the
	// notifications of a subscription to its notificationURI, which a
	// device chooses: DefaultNotificationURIAllowed when nil. A refused
	// subscription is answered 403.
	NotificationURIAllowed func(u *url.URL) bool
	// NotificationWorkers bounds the notifications sent at once: 16 when
	// zero.
	NotificationWorkers int
	// NotificationRetry decides whether a notification that could not be
	// delivered is sent again, and when: when nil, it is sent again while
	// the receiver is unreachable, fails (5xx) or times out, after a delay
	// that doubles from 1 s to 5 min, with jitter. A notification refused
	// with a 4xx, or not sent again, cancels its subscription.
	NotificationRetry ieee20305.RetryPolicy
	// NotificationCancelAfter cancels a subscription whose notifications
	// have failed for this long: 24 hours when zero.
	NotificationCancelAfter time.Duration
	// EventClock is the clock of the lifecycle of events (when they become
	// active): Clock, with timers of the operating system, when nil.
	EventClock schedule.Clock
	// OnResponse, when set, is called with each new Response a client
	// posts, and its href.
	OnResponse func(ctx context.Context, href string, response any)
	// MaxListItems caps the lists clients post to, such as LogEvents,
	// Responses and the Readings of mirrors: the oldest items beyond it are
	// deleted. 1000 when zero; no cap when negative. An operator's posts
	// are not capped.
	MaxListItems int
	// EventRetention is how long after its end the server keeps an event in
	// its scheduler (not in its store): 24 hours when zero.
	EventRetention time.Duration
	// FlowPolicy answers the FlowReservationRequests of devices: GrantAll
	// when nil.
	FlowPolicy FlowPolicy
	// Metrics receives the requests of the server (and, when it is one, its
	// notifications and event transitions), to count and time them; none
	// when nil.
	Metrics Metrics
	// Hooks override or extend the handling of resources, by WADL resource
	// ID; they run before the built-in function sets.
	Hooks map[string]Hooks
	// Logger receives the server's log (see ieee20305.Logger); none when
	// nil.
	Logger ieee20305.Logger
}
```

Config configures a Server. The zero value serves an empty resource tree with an in-memory store.

### type Hooks

```go
type Hooks struct {
	// Get returns the document of the resource, computed rather than
	// stored, such as Time.
	Get func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) (any, error)
	// Create handles a POST to the resource: by default, a POST to a list

	Create func(ctx context.Context, r *Request) (string, error)

}
```

Hooks are the handling of a resource beyond what the server does for any resource. A nil hook leaves the default. A hook that returns an \*HTTPError answers with its status.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	OnRequest(method string)
	OnResponse(method, resource string, status int, d time.Duration)
}
```

Metrics receives the requests of a server, to count and time them: set it as Config.Metrics. OnRequest is called when a request comes in, and OnResponse when it is answered, with the WADL resource ID of its target (such as "EndDeviceList"; "" for a path the server does not have), which makes a label of few values.

The methods are called synchronously from the goroutines that serve the requests: they must be safe for concurrent use, quick, and must not block. Embed NopMetrics to implement only some. A Metrics may also be a NotificationMetrics and an EventMetrics.

```go
type Node struct {
	// Href is the path of the resource, such as "/edev/3".
	Href string

	Owner string
	// Parent is the href of the resource or list the resource was created
	// in, if any. Deleting a node deletes the nodes whose Parent it is.
	Parent string
	// Modified is when the resource last changed.
	Modified time.Time
}
```

Node is a resource of the server: its href, its WADL resource, its value and who may read it.

### type Store

```go
type Store interface {
	// Get returns the node at href, or an error matching ErrNoNode.
	Get(ctx context.Context, href string) (*Node, error)
	// Put inserts or replaces the node at n.Href.
	Put(ctx context.Context, n *Node) error
	// Delete removes the node at href, the nodes created in it
	// (recursively), and its membership in lists.
	Delete(ctx context.Context, href string) error
	// AddMember makes the node at member an item of the list at list; a
	// member may belong to several lists.
	AddMember(ctx context.Context, list, member string) error
	// RemoveMember removes member from the list at list.
	RemoveMember(ctx context.Context, list, member string) error
	// Members returns the items of the list at list, in the order they were
	// added.
	Members(ctx context.Context, list string) ([]*Node, error)
	// Hrefs returns the hrefs of every node, sorted.
	Hrefs(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error)
}
```

Store holds the resources of a server. Its methods are safe for concurrent use, and it never hands out a value it holds itself: Get and Members return copies, and Put stores a copy.

#### func NewMemStore

```go
func NewMemStore(clone func(any) any) Store
```

NewMemStore returns a Store that keeps everything in memory. clone makes the deep copies of values: ieee20305.Clone when nil, or the Clone of a profile package, such as csipaus.Clone, for its documents.
